root_idea.summary: The root centers on marking, exposing, or pursuing a defect, yielding the meanings of blaming, fault-finding, and disparaging others.
root_idea.development: The lexical development includes an original nonverbal sign made with the eye, head, or lip, then extends to verbal blame and speaking ill of others. A separate Classical branch denotes pushing, repelling, or striking.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form لَمَزَ.
Displayed under the normalized nominal citation form لُمَزَةٌ rather than the inflected Quranic occurrence.

senses.definition: To blame, reproach, criticize, or find fault with someone or with what they have done.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic usage, this includes blaming someone concerning the distribution of alms and criticizing others; the action may be expressed directly to the person.

senses.definition: To speak ill of, disparage, or backbite another by exposing or mentioning faults.
senses.usage_conditions: The use may concern a person in their presence or absence. It denotes verbal detracting and fault-finding, not merely a nonverbal sign.

senses.definition: A habitual fault-finder or detractor; one who repeatedly speaks ill of others.
senses.usage_conditions: Applied to a man or woman; the ending ة is reported as expressing intensiveness rather than necessarily feminine gender. Classical descriptions differ over whether the fault-finding is done to the face or behind the back, and by tongue, eye, or other signs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a sign to someone with the eye or another feature, such as the head or lip, accompanied by low speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the reported original nonverbal signification of the verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To push, impel, or repel; also to strike or beat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct physical-action branch of the Form I verb in Classical Arabic.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Enigmatic or indirect conversation, or communication by signs, between two people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction is described as involving talking enigmatically and making signs with one another; مُلَامَزَةٌ is also reported as synonymous with مُلَاغَزَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who frequently makes signs with the eye or the like.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive agent noun formed from the nonverbal signification.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Persons who speak ill of others, even truthfully, in their presence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural lexical form described as referring to people who engage in this kind of direct verbal disparagement.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Covers blaming, reproaching, finding fault, and speaking ill of others.
Covers pushing, repelling, striking, and beating.
Covers enigmatic conversation and communication by signs.
Covers the intensive agent noun for habitual fault-finding and speaking ill.
Active-participle identification without an independent lexical definition.
Covers the plural form for persons who speak ill of others in their presence.

cautions: Classical descriptions give competing distinctions between هُمَزَةٌ and لُمَزَةٌ, including presence versus absence and tongue versus eye; the nominal sense therefore preserves their shared habitual-detractor core without selecting one disputed distinction.
The physical pushing or striking branch is Classical Arabic evidence and is not assigned to the Quranic Form I senses.
